sentences.text:
Author: M.Ganga Rao
Bench: M.Ganga Rao
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice M.Ganga Rao
 Writ Petition No.12091 Of 2017
Order:
The case of the petitioners is that they have established a water processing unit in the year 2011 as a proprietary firm and the same was closed on 09.03.2012 due to lack of market.
On the same day, the license granted by the Commercial Tax Officer, Rajahmundry has been cancelled.
On 16.03.2012 some unknown person said to be inspected the premises and collected some water bottles in the presence of watchman and sent it for analysis.

After receiving the analysis report from the laboratory on 11.02.2013 the second respondent ordered for prosecution on the complaint made by the third respondent before VII Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate, Rajahmundry, which is numbered as C.C.No.224 of 2017.

entities.text: VII Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate, Rajahmundry
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the sanction of prosecution dated 11.02.2013 under Section 3(1)(zz), 21, 26(2)(i) and 27(1) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, 'the Act) against the petitioners, is illegal and contrary to Sections 77 and 42 of the Act and Rules made thereunder.

Learned Assistant Government Pleader appearing for the respondents states that the then Food Safety officer inspected the petitioners' godown premises on 16.03.2012 by obtaining sanction on 13.03.2012.
On 07.04.2012 letter was received from Food Safety Designated Officer to the Commissioner of Food Safety, Andhra Pradesh for launching prosecution.

On 07.05.2013 Food Safety Officer filed a complaint before the Magistrate thereby the same was returned and resubmitted on 27.05.2016 and the same was returned on 31.05.2016 as per Section 77 of the Act and the complaint is numbered as C.C.No.224 of 2017 and there is no illegality in launching the prosecution against the petitioners under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act and Rules made thereunder much less in violation of provisions of Sections 77 and 42 of the Act.

In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the above submissions and on perusal of the record, this Court prima facie found that there is negligence on the part of the respondents in launching the prosecution against the petitioners and the Court has taken cognizance of the offence in the year 2017 and it is in violation of provisions of Section 77 of the Act and also contrary to the provisions of Section 42 of the Act.

Hence, the order of prosecution under Section 3(1)(zz), 21,
26(2)(i) and 27(1) of Food Safety and Standards Act dated 11.02.2013 and numbering of C.C.No.224 of 2017 is beyond time prescribed under the provisions of Section 77 of the Act.
